subject.title: [Slack] Agent lacks visibility into own channel messages from DM sessions

question: What authorization and retention contract should govern a Slack DM session reading the same agent’s outbound channel activity?
rationale: The implementation gap is clear, but repository behavior does not determine whether access should require current channel membership, which Slack identity performs authorization, how long content is retained, or whether deleted/edited messages remain queryable.

options.title: Scoped self-activity ledger
options.body: Record only canonical outbound activity and expose authorized same-agent, same-account Slack entries with bounded retention and deletion/edit handling.

options.title: Sibling session history access
options.body: Allow DM turns to query sibling Slack session transcripts, accepting a substantially broader content and authorization surface.

options.title: Preserve strict isolation
options.body: Keep current boundaries and make explicit shared memory or targeted session operations the supported cross-context workflow.

recommendation.title: Scoped self-activity ledger
recommendation.body: Record only canonical outbound activity and expose authorized same-agent, same-account Slack entries with bounded retention and deletion/edit handling.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior issue decision and recent Slack/session history make this the strongest available owner for the remaining product/security choice.
